title: No first-class Rust crate-extraction facility (monolith → workspace-member crate)
wanted_capability:
A reusable way to extract a cohesive subsystem out of a monolithic crate into a new workspace-member crate, as a guarded/transactional operation. Concretely: (1) scaffold the new crate — create crates/<name>/Cargo.toml ([package] + inferred [dependencies]) and src/lib.rs, add <name> to the root [workspace].members, and add <name> = { path = "crates/<name>" } to each named consumer's [dependencies]; (2) move the chosen modules/items into it with visibility bumped to pub at the new crate boundary; (3) crate-aware path rewrite — rewrite `crate::<seg>` / `use crate::<seg>` references in the origin crate to `<new_crate>::<seg>` (with use-tree splitting), and rewrite references from the extracted code back into the origin to `<origin_crate>::...`; (4) DAG guard — verify the extraction keeps the workspace dependency graph acyclic (this repo's contract-bottom invariant: implementation crates point down, never sideways/up); (5) validate via cargo check --workspace + rust_compile_fix_round with rollback across all writes. Ideal shape is a compound bbox_refactor_run macro `extract_rust_crate`, directly analogous to the existing `migrate_rust_mods_to_lib` macro but one level out (package→new-package instead of bin→lib), optionally fronted by a refactor atom for autonomous repeat use.</wanted_capability>
<parameter name="missing_primitive">A `extract_rust_crate` compound plan/macro (bbox_refactor_run) plus its three missing sub-primitives: a workspace-crate scaffolder (Cargo.toml + lib.rs + members + consumer dep-edge wiring), a crate-aware path rewriter (`crate::`/`use crate::` ↔ `<crate>::` with use-tree splitting, generalizing rewrite_rust_bin_crate_paths beyond the bin→lib case), and a workspace-DAG acyclicity check.</missing_primitive>
<parameter name="fallback_used">Hand-compose the sequence from existing within-crate primitives: write_file + multiple ensure_toml_table for scaffolding and dep wiring; rust_top_level_dependency_analysis to find the seam; extract_rust_items_to_submodule / move_rust_items_with_local_deps to move the cluster; migrate_rust_mods_to_lib / rewrite_rust_bin_crate_paths / move_rust_items_with_callers approximate the path rewrite (simple-name-segment match only, not crate-path aware, no use-tree splitting — leftovers need manual cleanup); rewrite_rust_*_visibility for the pub bump; bbox_refactor_run with cargo gates + rust_compile_fix_round to converge. No DAG cycle guard exists; relies on cargo check failing.</fallback_used>

notes:
extract_rust_crate facility need: peel cohesive subsystems off the 277k-LOC root `blackbox` crate (the release-build serial-frontend pole) into workspace crates. The facility = the migrate_rust_mods_to_lib transactional shape generalized: scaffolder + crate-aware path rewriter + workspace-DAG acyclicity guard. Below: the worked-campaign record + the trap catalog the facility must automate.

CAMPAIGN OF RECORD (code-intelligence cluster split). DAG: bbox-corpus-core (foundation: entity_ref, git, edit-DTOs FileEdit/TextEdit/sha256_hex/path_string, Language, LspConfig, ProjectRecord) <- bbox-chunker, bbox-lsp <- bbox-refactor <- bbox-code-nav <- (macros). STATUS: stages 0-3 DONE + merged to beta (root 277.7k->181k LOC). Stage 4 = extract syntax-nav lane of code_nav -> bbox-code-nav (dossier ready): split is function-interleaved in mod.rs (index-bound lane = code_symbols_indexed/indexed_kind_filter_for/indexed_handoff + 3 tantivy helpers STAY root behind a thin shim; live lane + semantic.rs MOVE); grammars finally leave root (code_nav uses only the tree-sitter runtime crate, grammars live in bbox-chunker); ProjectRecord stays root (re-export); managed_fleet_worktree_project moves with code_nav; design choice: ParseReport DTO coupling (keep in bbox-refactor vs lower to corpus-core). Stage 5 = macros.

TRAP CATALOG (accumulated across 5 worked extractions — what the facility must automate):
1. DEP ENUMERATION: scan inline-qualified `<crate>::` paths (not just `use`), route test-only deps to [dev-dependencies], AND grep the crate's OWN PACKAGE NAME `blackbox::` — a `crate::`-only scan misses upward edges written via the package name (git->blackbox::config; lsp->blackbox::{config::LspConfig, util::test_env_lock}). These make a module look like a leaf when it secretly reaches up.
2. UPWARD-EDGE INVERSION: a foundation module reaching up into root config/state -> invert via a startup-injected OnceLock (child exposes set_X() pub; root calls it once after load; env/default fallback preserves behavior). Used for git notes namespace.
3. CROSS-CRATE DERIVE-VERSION ALIGNMENT: a moved type that derives e.g. schemars::JsonSchema may need a DIFFERENT version of the derive crate than the root's direct dep (corpus-core needed schemars 1.x to match the MCP/tool schemas, not root's direct 0.8). cargo check surfaces this as a trait-version mismatch; the scaffolder should align derive-macro crate versions to whatever the moved derives actually resolve against.
4. cfg(test) HELPERS don't cross crate boundaries: test-only helpers consumed by the PARENT's tests need `#[cfg(any(test, feature="test-support"))]` + a parent dev-dep (vectors). But a test-only env lock used only WITHIN the moved crate's own tests is better replaced by a crate-LOCAL `static Mutex` (lsp, refactor) since cross-crate tests are separate processes.
5. FIXTURE / CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR-RELATIVE RESOURCES: moved tests that build paths from CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR with a hard-coded module path segment (e.g. "src/refactor/test_fixtures") break — the fixture dir moves with the crate but the literal segment must be updated to the new crate-relative path.
6. cargo fmt MULTI-TENANT OVER-REACH: `cargo fmt` in a shared/multi-crate tree reformats unrelated peer files; restore those (scoped) before committing — only the extraction surface should change.
7. RE-EXPORT ALIAS is the default low-churn caller strategy: `use <child> as <oldmod>;` (or `pub use`) in root lib.rs makes all `crate::<oldmod>::*` resolve unchanged (0 churn across 25+23+9+45+inbound sites). When lowering a TYPE, leave `pub use <child>::Type;` in its old home.
8. SELECTIVE pub PROMOTION is auto-driven: cargo check forces exactly the cross-boundary symbols to pub — including ones whose need only appears because a SIBLING root module uses them across the new boundary (stage 3's cargo check forced refactor::{parse_report,resolve_path} to pub because root's code_nav uses them). Wholesale pub(crate)->pub in a moved foundation file is acceptable.
9. SELF-PATH REWRITE: absolute `crate::<oldmod>::sub::X` inside moved code becomes `crate::sub::X`; re-export shims like `csharp/mod.rs` `pub(crate) use crate::refactor::{...}` become `pub(crate) use crate::{...}`.
10. ORPHAN RULE: move ALL inherent + trait impls of a moved type WITH the type (verified clean for the edit DTOs + all refactor types).

EXECUTION NOTE: stages 2-3 were executed by brodex gpt-5.5 bros in isolated git worktrees (cargo check as the gate), reviewed + independently re-validated + ff-merged by the orchestrator. Worked well for delicate multi-module surgery; the worktree cold-compiles (no shared target — that convention was retired).
